## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Kappaṭṭhakathā* (Kv 13.1) is a doctrinal debate located in the thirteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The discussion centers on the status of one who endures for a cosmic aeon (*kappattha*), a designation canonical sources apply to serious offenders such as schismatics (*saṅghabhedaka*) condemned to hell [Bareau 1955; SuttaCentral]. In early sectarian controversies, schools disputed whether an individual destined to endure for an aeon (*kappattha*) must persist for the full cosmic cycle, and whether such a person remains capable of generating wholesome consciousness (*kusala citta*) through acts such as offering donations or venerating a shrine [Bareau 1955]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation of the text in one language [SuttaCentral].

Doctrinally, the text is linked to canonical treatments of schism, including the *Paṭhamaānandasutta* (AN 10.39), the *Saṁghabheda Sutta* (Iti 18), the Vinaya *Saṁghabhedakakkhandhaka* (Kd 17), and the Chinese text T 765.9 [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects no cross-language matches with a score of 10 or greater, but records extensive Pali-internal text reuse comprising 145 matching passages across 13 other Kathāvatthu debates [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal reuse partners include the *Iddhibalakathā* (Kv 11.5, sharing 957 characters), the *Sabbamatthītikathā* (Kv 1.6, sharing 759 characters across 22 matches), and the *Adhigayhamanasikārakathā* (Kv 16.4, sharing 623 characters) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus agree on an explicit relationship between the *Kappaṭṭhakathā* and the *Asañciccakathā* (Kv 20.1), which share three matching segments totaling 351 characters [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
